correctness.rationale: Every Barber modularity matrix entry is computed exactly from the degrees. Its four-block sign table has strictly positive specialist–core and generalist–peripheral entries and strictly negative cross-block entries. Every partition has numerator at most the sum of positive entries; the stated two-module partition attains this sum and strictness proves uniqueness. Writing X=(p+q)a and Y=qb, the sharp bound follows from 4XY <= (X+Y)^2 with an explicit integer equality construction. The proof treats every positive parameter choice with p+q>=3. Exact checker verify.py independently optimized all 156 small profiles and all 2,279 partitions of seven selected small graphs; finite checks corroborate but do not prove the infinite claim.

value.rationale: Exact identification of the global bipartite community-detection optimum in the ecologically natural two-tier generalist/specialist family gives a concrete diagnostic for simultaneous neighborhood nesting and strong modularity. The sharp proportion-dependent ceiling and achievable near-one-half limit with arbitrarily many primary species are substantive, quantitative refinements not just a renamed two-row example. This does not allege significance in data or ecological dynamics, and perfect nesting refers to inclusion, not empirical tie-penalized NODF.
